alt: Text B of about 550 to 600 words is summarised in continuous writing of no more than 150 words, for 20 marks. “Select” is the reading half (R1 and R5, 10 marks): choose every relevant point and only those. “Present” is the writing half (W2 and W3, 10 marks): group and link the points in concise prose in your own words.
caption: Select earns the reading marks; present earns the writing marks.

alt: The summary process in five steps: find the focus, select the points, group and order them, write in your own words as continuous prose, and check the 150-word limit. The first two steps serve the reading marks and the next two the writing marks.
caption: Points first, then groups, then prose, then the word count.

alt: An anecdote about Maria, a nurse from Lisbon, saving on fuel is cut down to the point it illustrates: cycling saves money. A funnel shows every part of Text B that answers the focus being reduced by stripping examples, statistics and anecdotes and merging repeats, leaving eight to ten short notes.
caption: Keep the point, drop the illustration, and count each idea once.

after: ## Step 4: write in your own words
alt: Three methods for own-words summary writing: generalise (buses, trains and trams become public transport), compress (people who live in the area and the businesses that operate there become local residents and businesses) and re-structure separate sentences into one with a shared subject. Technical terms may stay; bullets and headings are not continuous writing.
caption: Generalise, compress and re-structure, and keep it as continuous prose.

alt: A word-count bar with 150 words marked as a ceiling. A summary well under it has probably missed points; one approaching it has all the points without detail; one over it has spent words on detail, and points after the limit are not credited. Count roughly by lines while writing and exactly at the end.
caption: Aim to approach 150 words, never to pass it.

alt: Eight benefit points from the school gardens text are grouped under pupils’ well-being, learning, and community and environment, and each group becomes one sentence of the model summary, linked by “also” and “too”. The drawbacks and the head teacher’s identity are excluded; the model runs to 74 words for the shortened text.
caption: Three groups become three linked sentences; drawbacks and detail stay out.

after: ## When the focus has two parts
alt: A two-part focus, such as the problems faced by volunteers and how they overcame them, is planned as two groups with points for each, written in separate sentences. Covering one aspect fully and the other in a single phrase misses reading marks.
caption: Plan a group for each part of the focus, and answer both in full.
